scope: A10 ten-class trusted baseline: source/split audit, per-image App-settings evaluation, ten-vs-nine comparable classes

environment.note: Local venv; no paid GPU or cloud worker.

limits: pHash and filename groups are candidate evidence, not scene truth.
The fixed legacy validation split was not re-split; clean_gate is a subset definition.
Macao and indoor CC BY images exist only in train, so they have no held-out validation.
Fresh door validation has no independent human adjudication and no fence positives.
Test split photos were not inferred or inspected in this audit.

method.input: independent float RGB half-pixel bilinear 640 letterbox, 114 padding

definition.all_val: 1,388 fixed validation records plus 15 fresh OID val
definition.legacy_val: fixed legacy validation split (leakage audited separately)
definition.fresh_oid_val: 15 frozen fresh OID door images, unseen by training
definition.clean_val: validation images with no train pHash group within radius 6

findings: Door is the weakest measured class: 5 TP / 3 FP / 34 FN at conf0.7 over 39 boxes in 29 images; recall 12.8% (95% CI 5.6-26.7), AP50 0.156.

17 of 27 positive door images never reach door score 0.30; 6 reach 0.70, but only 5 are TP and 2 are high-score localisation/matching false positives; one additional door-negative image is reported as door at 0.845.

Person on the strict subset: 98 TP / 19 FP / 179 FN at conf0.7; precision 83.8%, recall 35.4% (95% CI 30.0-41.2), AP50 0.573. The low recall is consistent with the user report, but bed/reflection/bag negatives are not yet measured.

Validation leakage is material: 279/1,403 (19.9%) validation images have a train pHash within 6; 23 share a train video group; there are no exact byte duplicates across splits. Stairs AP50 falls from 0.834 to 0.588 and caution from 0.980 to 1.000 with only 8 positive boxes after strict same-source filtering.

Fence cannot be evaluated: 10 validation images have fence coverage, 0 have a fence positive box, and 0 fence predictions occur at conf0.3/0.7 inside coverage. The 1,242 train fence boxes have no independent positive holdout.

Nine-class is higher than ten-class on all seven comparable classes at the clean subset (e.g. person 0.607 vs 0.573, bin 0.937 vs 0.884, escalator 0.811 vs 0.758 AP50). It has no door, fence or stairs and is an older pipeline, so it is not a fallback; it does show the ten-class additions did not improve the old classes.
Macao/indoor CC BY images (776) exist only in train, so their domain has no held-out validation.
No candidate, weight change, deployment or quality-gate pass is implied; the app remains 1.4.3+8 with 10-class experimental weights.
next_data_requirements: Door: at least 100 independent reviewed images/boxes across >=20 source groups, including small, distant, glass, double and partially occluded doors, with at least two confirmed negatives per positive.
Person: full-image hard negatives (bed, mirror/reflection, bag, mannequin, poster) and positives at measured 0.5/1/2/3 m; keep the original user scene separate and consented.
Fence: positive and negative holdout boxes; zero positive validation boxes currently exist.
Keep the strict subset and per-image report fixed; add data only after review, then rerun the same script without retuning on validation.
Do not start training, publish weights or deploy the review service from this baseline alone.
limits: Source PyTorch checkpoint, not an in-pass TFLite/phone-camera run; PT<->TFLite parity was verified separately at max abs 2.65e-5.
No NV12 camera capture, real HKDI scene, distance measurement or VoiceOver task evidence.
Labels are assistant-reviewed candidates, not independent human adjudication.
Door holdout is 29 images/39 boxes; confidence intervals are wide.
Nine-class training/selection history and possible validation exposure are not fully documented; comparison is directional only.
Legacy validation split was not re-split; clean and strict subsets are definitions, not a new official split.
Test-split images were not inferred or inspected.
